what: Why the stored exhaustion line and a step line's own 20-second flow differ at some first steps: every look-up of the two research tables made a second way, by place on the tape, and compared
asked: Greg, 2026-11-23, the handoff's second check: read the job's count of first steps where the stored exhaustion line equals the step line's own 20-second flow, and where it does not. The reason for the ones that do not is found here, not guessed.
nothing_applied: No window, no label, no average, no midpoint; nothing new calculated on the tape; nothing from another trade day.

the_two_ways.by_time: the last read made at or before the nanosecond of the tick (what the research threads job did)
the_two_ways.by_place: the last read made before that nanosecond, or at it and not after the tick on the tape; trades leaving at a nanosecond leave first

columns.what: Which move: trade leg, run of the best bid, run of the best ask.
The move, as the research table names it.
The tick of its first step: its position on the tape.
Size bought in the 20 seconds, as stored on the step line.
Size sold in the 20 seconds, as stored on the step line.
The figure made from those two: bought minus sold over bought plus sold.
The stored exhaustion line read by time: the last read at or before that nanosecond.
The stored exhaustion line read by place on the tape: the last read not after the tick.
The number of that read. Empty when no read had been made yet.
How many reads of the stored line share that nanosecond.
Yes when the read by place equals the step line's own figure.

checks.what: both stored lines are in time order; every stored value of the two research tables is the line (or the quote) read by time; the counts of equal and not equal first steps are the ones the research threads job wrote; every hump's moment is a read of the stored line
